literal: If they see a fitting opportunity, for striking, an anvil is the friendship of those who do not inwardly agree but outwardly associate closely.
translation: The friendship of those who do not inwardly agree but outwardly behave smoothly is like an anvil, serving only to hold you still until they find the fitting opportunity to strike.
modern: மனதால் ஒன்றாமல், வெளியில் மட்டும் நெருங்கிப் பழகுபவர்களின் நட்பு, தகுந்த சமயம் கிடைக்கும்போது நம்மை அடித்து வீழ்த்துவதற்குப் பயன்படும் பட்டடை போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against insincere friendship. The poet compares the friendship of insincere people—who pretend to be close but do not truly align in heart—to an anvil. Just as an anvil holds a piece of metal firmly in place only so that the hammer can strike it, these false friends maintain a close relationship only to keep you within reach until they find the perfect opportunity to strike and ruin you. The key words 'நேரா' (not inwardly agreeing) and 'நிரந்தவர்' (outwardly behaving smoothly) highlight the contrast between their inner hostility and outer friendliness.
